homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field; its capture relation notes that 'the address carries a disambiguator, the bare name being shared', and the operator added 'DeepMind' to the address (BRIEF-NEW-ROW-FIELD §5). The bare name is a homonym: Wikipedia's disambiguation opens with the Trojan hero (B8 F48) and lists, among others, 'Aeneas (biblical figure), a paralyzed man cured by Saint Peter in the Acts of the Apostles' (B8.wiki), a homonym inside the New Testament the field is organized around; the model is named after the hero (B1 F8, B5 F37), which keeps the hero a distinct entity and its namesake, never a sense of the model's name. Every D candidate in the archive (21 sentences in 8 deposits) is the hero's. T composes the target and no homonym (CAP-1-13). 'Predicting the Past' and predictingthepast.com are the entity's interface and alias (census aka); the Latin Epigraphic Dataset is its corpus, a distinct object.
distinct_entities: Aeneas, the Trojan hero (Virgil's Aeneid, Homer's Iliad), the model's namesake (B1 F8, B5 F37); the archive's Aeneas (#288, #1102, #1271, #1289–#1293, #1684)
Aeneas of Acts 9:33–34, the paralysed man healed by Peter (Wikipedia's disambiguation, B8.wiki)

Ithaca, DeepMind's model for ancient Greek inscriptions (2022), which Aeneas builds upon and which was upgraded to be powered by Aeneas (B1 F8, F17); the census's neighbour (RF-23); its /non row, if one is built, is a distinct row
the Latin Epigraphic Dataset (LED), the model's corpus, and its sources, the Epigraphic Database Roma, the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg and the Epigraphik-Datenbank Clauss–Slaby (B1 F11, B5)
Google DeepMind, the operator; the University of Nottingham, the co-developer; Warwick, Oxford and AUEB, partners; Durham University, on the interface card only (F45)
the Res Gestae Divi Augusti and the Monumentum Ancyranum; the Mainz votive altars (CIL XIII, 6665), the paper's case studies
the other Aeneases of the disambiguation page (Aeneas Tacticus, Aeneas of Gaza, Aeneas Silvius, places, ships, a telecom provider, a GNU package)

captures.description: AENEAS, BY THE OPERATOR'S ADDRESS 'AENEAS DEEPMIND', ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'an artificial intelligence model developed by Google DeepMind (introduced in July 2025) designed to contextualize, restore, date, and locate ancient, damaged, or fragmentary Latin inscriptions.' The Latin Epigraphic Dataset ('over 176,000 inscriptions'), the multimodal input, gap restoration, dating 'within roughly 13 years', the historians' trial (90%, 44%), the Predicting the Past interface. Seven cards: DeepMind, the Google blog, Oxford's Faculty of Classics, GitHub, Nature, Predicting the Past, MIT Technology Review.

atoms.evidence: In testing with historians, Aeneas provided useful contextual parallels 90% of the time
